title: Training an AI to control a human body so I can create realistic looking enemies
author: argidev
selftext:
The plan is to teach an AI to learn how to walk, then build a game around it.

Would you play a game like this?

replies.author: argidev
replies.body: Never heard of that game, and google doesn't seem to provide anything closely resembling this. Could you share a link to the game or a trailer?

replies.author: Inside_Ease3366
replies.body: Its a physics engine that rockstar acquired https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HWJRzABRNvo

replies.author: argidev
replies.body: WOW! I've never seen this before, but that's precisely what I'm going for. Realistic simulations of the human body. The idea was to create a humanoid body that would learn how to balance itself and later learn to walk and run, so that it could chase you as a player, creating much more realistic zombie like enemies, which you'd have to defend yourself against. Imagine a hoard of zombies coming towards you, crouching to duck your bullets, and even hopping or crawling after you remove any of it's limbs. This is still wishful thinking, but if I somehow manage to pull this off and teach them how to stand up and walk, these would create much more realistic and believable   movements, that no other game I know of offers. Except Euphoria apparently....

comments.author: Bobobarbarian
comments.body: How do you build a game around what is effectively an animation system? Not being facetious, genuinely don’t understand unless it’s like a QWOP situation

replies.author: thetinytrex
replies.body: My question exactly.  Like a game with realistic moving enemies? Thats a lot of games bro... not really a selling point to build a game around.

replies.author: argidev
replies.body: I figured having an actual brain controlling a body would create much more realistic looking enemies, so I wouldn't have to rig the individual poses. But this has started more out of my own curiosity, whether I could teach a brain to control a humanoid body, the game idea only came later, as I was trying to figure out any practical use-cases for this project.

replies.author: Bobobarbarian
replies.body: It’s certainly an interesting tech demo (I think Nvidia is doing something similar if you haven’t looked into it), and it could definitely have some use cases

replies.author: argidev
replies.body:
Nvidia's Omniverse is precisely what made me look into this...

And I've actually experimented with something similar before, but I tried teaching an AI to control a simpler body, before tackling this more complex one. [https://petrecelvlad.github.io/Origami/](https://petrecelvlad.github.io/Origami/)

comments.author: Unlikely_Perspective
comments.body: Are these real days of your gpu chugging away? I would look a bit more into your training methodology, this doesn’t look too practical at the current speed, cool experiment though.

replies.author: argidev
replies.body: That's not exactly training over 30 days, it's more like the progress I've achieved over that period. I kept making a lot of tweaks and changes to how the brain would learn, adding various crutches and aids to help them stand up. After one month however, I finally figured a formula that works, and the actual training period is more like 3 days. And I'm training them on a 15 years old PC with a built in graphics cards, so processing is done by CPU not GPU.
